## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 28, titled *Accekacīvara* ("Storing haste-cloth too long"), is a monastic legal text belonging to the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a monk who retains or stores an "urgent robe" (*accekacīvara*) beyond the allowable time limit commits an offense that requires relinquishment of the robe and formal confession [SuttaCentral]. The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali, along with translations into four other modern languages listed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral indicate extensive preservation across early Buddhist traditions [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali Vinaya, corresponding formulations are found in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (NP 28), the Bhikkhu Parivāra (NP 28), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (NP 29), the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (NP 29), and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra (NP 29) [SuttaCentral]. Parallels in other Vinaya lineages include Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Lokottaravāda Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga texts preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies substantial shared material across the Pali corpus, displaying prominent overlaps with Khandhaka texts—particularly the Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka (Kd 3), Senāsanakkhandhaka (Kd 16), Uposathakkhandhaka (Kd 2), and Mahākhandhaka (Kd 1)—as well as related robe-rules in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (notably Bu-Vb NP 3, NP 29, NP 21, and NP 1) and commentary/sub-commentary treatises such as the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also establishes cross-language alignments with Tibetan translations of the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2) and *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005), as well as the Sanskrit *Vinayasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
